paper_title: Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models
caption: The effect of context masking perturbations by tag. Error bars indicate the standard deviation.
model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the effect of context masking perturbations on multilingual BERT models, broken down by four morphosyntactic tags—case, gender, number, and tense—along the horizontal axis, with the vertical axis labeled “effect” ranging from 0 to 20 in linear increments. Each tag category contains six grouped bars representing different model variants: mBERT-L₂ (light blue), XLM-L₂ (dark blue), mBERT-R₂ (light green), XLM-R₂ (dark green), mBERT-B₂ (light red), and XLM-B₂ (dark red), as indicated by the legend in the upper right. Error bars extending vertically from each bar represent the standard deviation of the effect measurement. For the “case” tag, mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ show the highest effects, approximately 12 and 11 respectively, while mBERT-L₂ and XLM-L₂ are around 6 and 5.5. For “gender,” mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ again lead with effects near 4 and 3.5, while other models hover near 1–2. In “number,” all models show low effects, mostly under 3, with mBERT-B₂ and XLM-B₂ slightly higher (~2.5). For “tense,” all models show minimal effects near or below 1, with XLM-B₂ slightly elevated at ~0.8. The bars are grouped by tag and not sorted by height, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond color coding.
